4 ازهر He made a fire, (S, K,) and a lamp, (A,) to give light, to shine, or to shine brightly. (S, A, K.) ―
-b2- أَزْهَرْتَ زَنْدِى [lit., Thou hast made my piece of stick, or wood, for producing fire to emit shining fire, or abundant fire; meaning, (tropical:) thou hast made me to accomplish my want: see 1]. (A.) ―
-b3- ازهر (AHn, T, S, M, A, Msb, [and so in the CK and in my MS. copy of the K, but SM says that in all the copies of the K it is written ↓ اِزْهَرَّ , like اِحْمَرَّ,]) It (a plant, or herbage, S, K, &c., and a tree, TA) flowered, or blossomed; (AHn, T, S, Msb, &c.;) as also ↓ زَهَرَ , aor.
زَهَرَ ; (Msb;) and ↓ ازهارّ . (AHn, K.) ―
-b4- أَزْهَرَتِ الأَرْضُ, and ↓ زَهَرَت , The land abounded with flowers. (Zj, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
